# Agent City Title Card — Creative Brief

## Objective
Create a six-second silent title card for Agent City that feels precise, modern, and transparent while making the supplied copy immediately legible.

## Audience
Software users watching a short Agent City showcase.

## Format
- Canvas: 640 × 360
- Frame rate: 30 fps
- Duration: 6 seconds / 180 frames
- Audio: None

## Exact Copy
- `AGENT CITY`
- `REAL AGENTS. VISIBLE WORK.`

No other claims, dialogue, labels, or supporting copy may appear.

## Creative Direction
Use a solid navy background, bright-blue original vector borders, and white system-monospace typography. The composition should feel architectural and deliberate: crisp rectangular geometry, restrained motion, high contrast, and generous spacing.

The title reveal completes by 0.5 seconds (frame 15), then remains readable. The second line begins its introduction at exactly 2 seconds (frame 60), settles quickly, and remains visible with the title through the final frame. Motion must not interfere with reading.

## Timeline
- Frames 0–14 / 0.000–0.500 s: Bright-blue border draws on while `AGENT CITY` reveals; the title is fully visible by frame 15.
- Frames 15–59 / 0.500–2.000 s: Hold the complete title in a stable composition.
- Frames 60–179 / 2.000–6.000 s: Introduce `REAL AGENTS. VISIBLE WORK.` at frame 60, settle it by frame 69, then hold both lines through the end.

## Production Boundaries
- Build only with original CSS/SVG shapes and system monospace typography.
- Do not use logos, external media, downloaded fonts, voice, music, sound effects, paid generation, or invented software capabilities.
- Do not imply licensing, rendering, review, or approval has already occurred.
- Final production still requires an actual render and independent review.

## Planning Acceptance Criteria
- The plan covers all 180 frames without gaps or overlaps.
- Both supplied lines are reproduced exactly.
- `AGENT CITY` is fully readable by frame 15.
- The second line begins at frame 60 and both lines remain visible through frame 179.
- The design uses only the specified colors, original vector geometry, and a system monospace font stack.
- No external production-media requirements are introduced.

# Style Plan

## Visual System
- Background: solid navy.
- Accent: one bright blue used for original vector borders and any minimal geometric rule work.
- Typography: white system monospace only, using a fallback stack such as `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace`.
- Geometry: original CSS/SVG rectangles and straight lines with crisp edges.
- Texture: none.
- Logos or external imagery: none.

## Composition
Place the copy within a bright-blue rectangular border inset safely from the 640 × 360 canvas edges. Center the title optically rather than relying only on mathematical centering. Set `AGENT CITY` as the dominant line with generous tracking. Place `REAL AGENTS. VISIBLE WORK.` beneath it at a smaller size with enough vertical separation to preserve hierarchy.

Maintain high contrast and safe margins. Avoid tiny text, excessive tracking, glows, gradients, faux interface elements, or details that imply unsupported product capabilities.

## Motion Language
Motion is linear, restrained, and frame-aligned.

- Frames 0–14: Draw or wipe on the bright-blue border while revealing the title with a small opacity/position settle.
- Frame 15: Title and border are complete.
- Frames 15–59: Static readability hold.
- Frames 60–69: Reveal the second line using a subtle opacity increase and short upward settle.
- Frames 70–179: Static hold of both lines and border.

Do not use camera movement, simulated depth, elastic easing, flicker, rapid cuts, or a closing fade. The final frame should retain the complete composition.

## Copy Rules
The only permitted text is:

```text
AGENT CITY
REAL AGENTS. VISIBLE WORK.
```

Capitalization and punctuation must remain exact.

## Production Notes
All visible elements can be authored directly as CSS/SVG and text. No external asset acquisition is required. Rendering and independent review remain downstream production requirements and are not represented as completed here.
